title: Aba, ima, bayit
topic: א ב בּ ת י; the vowels a and i; you (m. and f.)
why: Four more letters (including the silent letter א and the two sounds of ב) and the vowel i, to read family words and say "you" to a man or to a woman.

{"lessons": ["

Four new letters

LetterNameSound
אalefsilent: it only carries the vowel
בּbetb (with the dot)
בvetv (without the dot)
תtavt
יyody

אַ is read simply a: the letter א makes no sound at all, it just holds the vowel.

The dot in בּ is called the dagesh. It changes the sound: בּ = b, ב = v. The v in \"Tel Aviv\" is a ב without a dot.

", "

The vowel i and the family

A dot under the letter is read i (like the ee in see): מִ = mi. It's often followed by a י: מִי (who?).

אִמָּאima: mom
אַבָּאaba: dad

Israelis, adults included, call their parents this way. There is no verb \"to be\" in the present tense: you say \"dad at-the-home\".

אַבָּא בַּבַּיִת.Dad is at home. [aba ba-bayit]

בְּ (in, at) attaches to the word; with the article \"the\", it becomes בַּ: בַּבַּיִת, at home (literally \"in the house\"); בַּיָּם, at the sea.

", "

You: אַתָּה or אַתְּ?

To say \"you\", Hebrew first asks: are you talking to a man or to a woman?

HebrewPronunciationMeaning
אַתָּהatayou (to a man)
אַתְּatyou (to a woman)
אַתְּ בַּבַּיִת?Are you at home? (to a woman) [at ba-bayit?]

Two words to recognize right away: כֵּן (ken, yes) and לֹא (lo, no).

Shabbat (שַׁבָּת) begins on Friday evening. People greet each other with שַׁבָּת שָׁלוֹם [shabbat shalom], \"a peaceful Shabbat\".
